P1.evidence: Internal call between the closer and his setter. No prospect present, so the sales process does not apply to any phase.

P5.evidence: No prospect. Worth noting in passing that the rep rehearsed a consequence frame for an upcoming call unprompted — for a 23-year-old firefighter, 'imagine yourself in five years still running in a building and you're just too exhausted to save someone's life' — which shows he knows the phase well when he plans for it.

P11.evidence: No close attempted; no prospect present.

objection_plays.detail: Not an objection on this call, but a prospect objection was relayed verbatim and is worth logging because the script has no answer for it. Bo Reid texted: 'I know the call you want me to get on to is just a closer slash salesman trying to get me to commit to paying for a plan. I'd rather not wait a week if one of the options are right for me. Can you email me the plan option info?' The setter's scripted reply was that there is no standard menu of plans and everything is custom, then offered to hand him to an 'advisor'. This is a pre-call transparency objection — the buyer wants prices before investing an hour with a closer — and it is the third instance of a demand for pre-purchase information in this batch, alongside Edward Garcia and Omar. The rep's plan to handle it was a WhatsApp voice note, on the theory that 'that builds so much more trust', which is instinct rather than script.

notes: Not scoreable as a sales call, and it should drop out of any adherence rollup. Three things a manager should take from it anyway. The setter is knowingly passing leads that fail financial qualification because they fit on profile, with a cheaper tier as the intended landing spot — which means the ICP income criterion is already being overridden upstream of the closer. The team tells prospects there is no standard price menu, which is not what the transcripts in this batch show. And the rep pre-emptively named 'Richard was too pushy' as a possible loss reason for a prospect he had spoken to the day before, which is worth holding next to the Rudolph and Geoffrey calls where he asked for payment repeatedly after being declined.
